clue.text: Offhand royalist

explanation.surface: A royalist behaving in a careless, offhand way.
explanation.definitionFit: Cavalier means casually dismissive, and the Cavaliers were the supporters of Charles I in the English Civil War.

clue.text: Hold in close affection

parts.note: read literally as holding someone in your arms lovingly, not merely being fond of them

explanation.definitionFit: To hug someone tenderly is to clasp them close as a sign of love.

clue.text: What he sees is immaterial

parts.note: a person whose sights are not physical things but dreams and imagined futures

explanation.definitionFit: A dreamer or seer perceives ideas and imaginings rather than solid objects.

clue.text: Rings to fix a reel up

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: a reel for thread or film is a spool

explanation.surface: Instructions for attaching rings so a fishing reel stays in place.
explanation.definitionFit: Loops are circular shapes, as rings are.

clue.text: Refreshed as sleep passes away

indicators.note: the letters are freshened up into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Feeling refreshed as a night's sleep drifts by.
explanation.walkthrough: 'passes away' is not dying here: time that slips by elapses.
explanation.definitionFit: Time that goes by is said to elapse, slipping past.

clue.text: He won't buy the same article twice

definitions.text: He won't buy the same article twice

parts.words: He won't buy the same article twice
parts.note: article means a piece of writing submitted to a newspaper, not goods in a shop

explanation.definitionFit: A newspaper's chief accepts or pays for pieces of writing, and would not take a piece already printed.

clue.text: River authority as a sporting target

parts.note: the Dart is a river in Devon, England
a governing board is an authority

explanation.surface: A river authority turned into a sports target.
explanation.definitionFit: Darts players aim at a round board marked with scoring segments.

clue.text: A voice of course

explanation.surface: A voice, naturally.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenor is a high male singing voice, and tenor also means the general course or drift of something.

clue.text: Have another think about seas breaking over ship

indicators.note: in a down clue, over places the anagram above the ship

parts.note: re means about or concerning

indicators.note: seas breaking means the letters are broken up and rearranged

parts.note: SS is the abbreviation for steamship

explanation.surface: Reconsidering after waves crash over a vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breaking' rearranges SEAS into ASSE, and 'over' sets it above SS in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: To reconsider is to evaluate something again.

clue.text: I'd set about ally so false

indicators.note: the letters are set about, arranged anew in a different order

explanation.surface: Someone attacking their partner, which seems treacherous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set about' looks like 'attacked' but rearranges the letters of I'D, ALLY and SO.
explanation.definitionFit: A false friend is unfaithful or treacherous.

clue.text: A girl graduate about to burst into tears

indicators.note: about means the graduate's letters go round the tears

parts.note: BA is a Bachelor of Arts
tears as a verb, rips, gives rend

explanation.surface: A young woman with a degree who is on the verge of crying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tears' reads as weeping, but it is the verb meaning rips; 'to burst into' is surface dressing that links the parts.
explanation.definitionFit: Brenda is a woman's first name.

clue.text: Id look up to one who's worshipped

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: in a down clue, up reverses the word for look

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look or behold

explanation.surface: The ego's id gazing upward at someone it worships.
explanation.definitionFit: An idol is a figure of devotion or adoration.

clue.text: Observes appearances

explanation.surface: Someone noticing how things look.
explanation.definitionFit: Looks as a verb means watches, and as a noun means a person's outward appearance.

clue.text: Border poet's whiskers

parts.note: a side is an edge or border
Robert Burns is Scotland's national poet

explanation.surface: The facial hair of a poet from the Scottish Borders.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Border' suggests the Scottish Borders region, apt for Burns, but just means side.
explanation.definitionFit: These are strips of hair grown down the cheeks, a kind of whiskers.

clue.text: Ecclesiastical vestments may hide them

indicators.note: may hide says the two words conceal a run of letters inside them

explanation.surface: Clerical robes covering a priest's lower legs.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition too: a cassock's hem covers the backs of the lower legs, and the same words conceal the answer across 'ecclesiastiCAL VEStments'.
explanation.definitionFit: These are the fleshy backs of the lower legs, which an ankle-length cassock conceals.

clue.text: Wicked, embraced Virginia, bubbly required

indicators.note: embraced means the state's abbreviation is held inside the word for wicked

parts.note: wicked means vicious
VA is the abbreviation for the US state of Virginia

explanation.surface: A wicked man holding Virginia, champagne in demand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bubbly' looks like champagne but describes a lively person.
explanation.definitionFit: A bubbly person is lively and full of high spirits.

clue.text: Casual footwear for bakers?

explanation.surface: Relaxed shoes for those who work in a bakery.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that bakers are taken as people who make loaves.
explanation.definitionFit: Slip-on shoes have this name, and a baker could be called one who makes loaves.

clue.text: How rain falls to form hard water

indicators.note: the letters are used to form a new word

explanation.surface: Rain falling and becoming hard water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hard water' (water with lots of minerals) is the anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Rain falls downwards, towards the ground.

clue.text: Cricket side and ground not in tune

parts.note: the off side is one half of a cricket field
a pitch is a playing ground

explanation.surface: A cricket team and its field sounding out of tune.
explanation.definitionFit: Singing flat or sharp means the notes are wrong, not matching the key.

clue.text: Carriage capsized at road crossing

parts.note: a fly is a light horse-drawn carriage for hire
a capsized boat is turned over

explanation.surface: A carriage overturning at a road junction.
explanation.definitionFit: A bridge carrying one road above another forms a crossing.

clue.text: Playboy with nothing to feel sorry about

indicators.note: about means the regret word goes round the nothing

parts.note: to rue is to regret or feel sorry
O looks like a zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A playboy feeling no remorse.
explanation.definitionFit: A rake is a dissolute pleasure-seeking man, a debauchee.

clue.text: Holy commands

explanation.surface: Sacred instructions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Holy' points to holy orders, the ranks of clergy.
explanation.definitionFit: Holy orders are the status of ordained clergy, and orders are also instructions given by someone in charge.

clue.text: Ring through at one point for work

parts.note: a ring is O-shaped
per means through or by means of
taken as written
E is east, one point of the compass

explanation.surface: Telephoning through at a particular moment to do a job.
explanation.definitionFit: A machine that functions or runs is said to work.

clue.text: Win, possibly earned

indicators.note: possibly signals the letters could be arranged another way

explanation.surface: A victory that may have been deserved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Win' is a verb here, as in win someone over.
explanation.definitionFit: To win someone's affection is to make yourself liked by them.

clue.text: Used for getting in the drink — after opening time

definitions.text: Used for getting in the drink — after opening time

parts.words: Used for getting in the drink — after opening time
parts.note: getting in the drink means dropping into the sea, and opening time is when the canopy opens, not when the pub does

explanation.definitionFit: Airmen ditching over water descend under an opened canopy of silk.

clue.text: Put a curb round gelding's head and get control

indicators.note: round means the curb word goes round the letter

parts.note: to rein is to curb or restrain

indicators.note: head means the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: Restraining a gelding at the head to master it.
explanation.definitionFit: A monarch's rule over a realm is power and control.

clue.text: An embrace for Lady Grey

indicators.note: embrace means the two letters hold the word for lady inside them

parts.note: she stands for a female person

explanation.surface: A hug for Lady Grey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lady Grey' reads as a name (Lady Jane Grey, or the tea), but Grey is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A face drained of colour is pale and grey.

clue.text: Quick breathing

explanation.surface: Rapid breaths.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quick' is the old sense, as in the quick and the dead.
explanation.definitionFit: Quick once meant living, and breathing shows a creature is living.

clue.text: A tradesman has trouble occupying a high position

indicators.note: occupying means the trouble sits inside the high position

parts.note: a tor is a rocky hill
to ail is to trouble

explanation.surface: A merchant with problems in a senior role.
explanation.walkthrough: TOR is a rocky hilltop, common on Dartmoor in England.
explanation.definitionFit: A maker of suits is a craftsman who sells his work.

clue.text: Banter becomes hurtful in time

parts.note: bad means harmful or hurtful
taken as written
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: Teasing that turns nasty over time.
explanation.definitionFit: Playful teasing talk, witty repartee.

clue.text: He's not bent but on the level

indicators.note: bent means twisted out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A man insisting he is not crooked but straight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bent' looks like slang for crooked, fitting the surface, but it rearranges HE'S NOT.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who is truthful and fair is said to be straight, not crooked.

clue.text: Back one aiming to retain his title

definitions.text: one aiming to retain his title

explanation.surface: A champion fighting back to keep his crown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back' is the football sense, a player in defence.
explanation.definitionFit: A back is a defensive player in football, and a champion holding a title against challengers also bears this name.
